sections.what: Describes the stage data received from the server: the stage order, and for each stage its status, times, summary and log.
sections.why: Describes what the server sends for the run page.

sections.name: RS_STAGES

sections.what: Lists each known stage with its friendly name, icon and description, from resolving scope through building the deck.

sections.watch_out: The build-deck description says results are recorded against each project in the Yard. Any change to that behaviour must update this text.

sections.name: TOTAL_LABELS
sections.title: Totals labels
sections.what: Maps the totals from the finalize stage to readable labels and colour tones, such as verified, unconfirmed, unreachable and not available.
sections.why: Likely reason: the counts are shown to the user with plain labels.
sections.watch_out: Only the listed totals are shown, so a new total from the server will not appear.

sections.name: ResolveBody
sections.title: Resolved scope list
sections.what: Draws each resolved scope item with its project count, mode and a small bar scaled to the largest count.
sections.why: Likely reason: a visual summary of what the scope covers.
sections.watch_out: The largest count is never below one, which prevents division by zero for an empty list.

sections.name: buildScanTrackStages
sections.title: Staged view builder
sections.what: Builds the staged view for each stage, adding findings from its summary. Resolve and finalize stages get custom content, and a finished finalize stage with a result links to the analysis view. Unknown stages get a generic label.
sections.why: Likely reason: the staged view gives a quick summary of each step. Not fully stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The analysis link appears only when finalize succeeds and has a result, so a failed finalize shows no link.

sections.name: buildScanProcessStages
sections.title: Process view builder
sections.what: Turns each known stage's log into readable trace lines, dropping timestamps and start or finish lines. Each line is sorted as a warning, a reading, a result, or a plain step. The comment says nothing is invented.
sections.why: The comment states the purpose: show only what was actually logged.
sections.watch_out: Sorting depends on text patterns, and a stage key missing from the known table is left out entirely.

summary: Gives each Reality Scan stage a readable name, icon and description, and turns the server's stage records into the data shown on the run page.
purpose: Lets the run page show friendly step names, counts, and a readable log instead of internal stage keys and raw text.
why: Likely reason: the stage names are internal, and the code also needs to handle older stage names. The second view explicitly says it invents nothing.
how: It keeps a table of known stage names and descriptions. One builder creates the staged view, adding findings, the scope list, and a link to analysis when finalize succeeds. A second builder reads each stage's stored log and sorts each line into a warning, a result, a reading, or a plain step, after removing timestamps and start or finish lines.
inputs: The run's stage order and stage records from the server, plus the run ID for links.
outputs: Stage objects for the staged view and process view, with labels, icons, status, findings and trace lines.
risks: Line sorting relies on text patterns in the logs, so a reworded server message can change its category. A stage key missing from the known table is dropped from the process view.
debug: If a stage shows the wrong name, compare its stage key with the known table. If trace lines are missing, check the log text format in the stored record.
